candidates.title: Uarch-step verifiers (C++ replay and regenerated Solidity step) accept uarch stores that the native uarch refuses as traps, although the log alone (the store address) authenticates the trap condition
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step regenerated from audit/prt2 (UArchStep.sol/EmulatorCompat.writeWord/AccessLogs.writeWord), as called by Dave CartesiStateTransition; also the C++ uarch_replay_state_access (machine::verify_step_uarch)
candidates.role: Referee verifier (regenerated machine-solidity-step); Dave CartesiStateTransition inherits it (referee model, rated by the copy's role); C++ verify_step_uarch is Support
candidates.location: src/uarch-replay-state-access.hpp do_write_word/check_write_word_access (no address-class check); src/machine.cpp machine::write_word 2030-2075 and machine::write_reg (x0, mvendorid, marchid, mimpid, uarch_x0 throw 'register is read-only'; unknown shadow slots throw 'unhandled write to shadow state'/'shadow uarch state'; non-memory or protected ranges throw); bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src/EmulatorCompat.sol writeWord -> AccessLogs.writeWord (no check); src/uarch-step.cpp writeUint64/executeSD..SB
candidates.description: Natively, a uarch store goes through machine::write_word, which refuses (throws, i.e. a uarch trap under R3: 'an access that its memory map does not allow') a store to: the uarch x0 shadow word (0x400018), the read-only main registers x0/mvendorid/marchid/mimpid in the shadow, any unknown slot of the shadow registers or shadow uarch state (e.g. the revert-root-hash word 0xfe0), the fixed protected ranges (shadow TLB, PMA table), the empty gaps inside the uarch-state node, and any address with no memory range (e.g. above 2^56). The log producers (uarch_record_state_access) and the computation-hash builder (collect_uarch_cycle_hashes_state_access) therefore refuse these steps. Both log verifiers instead accept them: uarch_replay_state_access::do_write_word and the Solidity AccessLogs.writeWord only check that the logged address equals the computed address and that the leaf proof matches, then define a successor that writes the value into the hash tree. Every one of these conditions is a function of the store address only (plus the fixed layout constants of the protocol version), and that address is computed from authenticated log data (the uarch registers and the instruction word), so the log already authenticates the trap. Accepting it gives a successor to a state that the state transition function says has none; e.g. after the accepted store to uarch x0, later verified steps that read rs1=x0 see 0xdeadbeef, a trajectory no native path can produce.
candidates.trigger: A dishonest claimant in a uarch-level match whose agreed before-state (or the state its fabricated uarch claim passes through) has a non-pristine uarch whose next instruction is such a store; it submits the crafted log to winLeafMatch / CartesiStateTransition.transitionState.
candidates.reachability: Believed unreachable. Every mcycle starts from the pristine uarch (uarch reset closes each mcycle and the valid template is at a pristine uarch); uarch RAM and the uarch shadow are outside every PMA so the guest cannot change them (R8); hence only the pristine uarch program executes, and it writes main registers only through writable shadow slots, the TLB only through the write-TLB ecall, and memory only after its own PMA checks. If the pristine program ever performed one of these stores from a reachable state, that would itself be the Critical case of R3 ('A pristine uarch program must never trap from a reachable state'). A1 requires the before-hash to be agreed by the honest claim, so in a match against the honest claim the before-state is canonical (reachable).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. The trigger is a crafted access log, which section 4 makes adversarial ('Logs and proofs are adversarial'); no exclusion of section 8 applies.

2 Role: the regenerated machine-solidity-step is a 'Referee verifier' (AUDIT.md Components: 'machine-solidity-step ... with its generated code and constants regenerated from audit/prt2 | Referee verifier'). Dave's CartesiStateTransition only inherits the defect from that copy ('A defect it only inherits from a copy of a verifier that it calls is rated by that copy's role'). The C++ verify_step_uarch is Support ('Off-chain verifiers ... | Support').

3 High/Medium cases: matches High: 'A verifier that misbehaves only on demonstrably unreachable before-states. Misbehaving means being nondeterministic, accepting a wrong or second after-hash (such as accepting a uarch trap, R3)'. The violated rule is R3: 'A verifier refuses a trap whenever the log it receives already authenticates the condition.' Here the condition depends only on the authenticated store address, so this is not the excused case ('Detecting any other trap would need the verifier to authenticate extra state'). Unreachability argument as in 'reachability'.

4 Critical: only if some input sequence from a valid template made the pristine uarch execute such a store (then 'A verifier defect that lets some log be accepted, for a reachable before-state, with an after-hash other than the canonical one', and independently R3's Critical pristine-uarch trap). No such path is known.

5 Low: n/a. The C++ copy alone would be Medium as Support ('A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'), but the referee verifier shares it, so High.
candidates.threat_to_goal: It removes the R3 margin that the referee refuses every trap it can see: the goal then depends entirely on the unproven property that no reachable state leads the pristine uarch to such a store. If any such path exists (a uarch program bug), the referee would settle a successor of a trapping state instead of refusing it, so a dishonest claim could win with a state that the transition function does not define.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R3/x0store.lua (lua5.4 with bugs/env.sh, against the shared EVM step harness on 8546). Before-state: 1 MiB RAM machine, uarch_pc=0x80000000 holding 'sd x1,0x18(x2)', x1=0xdeadbeef, x2=0x400000 (store to uarch x0). Native m:run_uarch(1) and m:log_step_uarch() both fail with 'register is read-only'. A hand-built 9-access log (proofs from m:get_proof) is accepted by cartesi.machine:verify_step_uarch with after-hash 0xe49b47d7...f3ea, and by the regenerated Solidity StepVerifier.step with the same after-hash 0xe49b47d73e0860058b0b544b599a27c6e012717328729d050b6272a7590ef3ea.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: build the before-state above, assert native run_uarch traps, craft the log as in x0store.lua, and require that cartesi.machine:verify_step_uarch raises and that evm_step e:step returns ok=false (and/or CartesiStateTransition.transitionState reverts on the released Dave build). Exit 1 while either verifier accepts. Variants: store to the marchid shadow address, to 0xfe0 (revert root hash slot) and to the shadow TLB with a plain sd.

candidates.title: On-chain step verifier rejects any access to the last 32-byte leaf of the address space (Memory.validateStrideLength off-by-one), which the native uarch, the C++ log producer and the C++ verifier accept
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step Memory.sol (unchanged since v0.17.0-test1; same file in the regenerated step and in Dave's machine/step)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src/Memory.sol validateStrideLength: assert(Stride.unwrap(stride) * s < MAX_STRIDE) with MAX_STRIDE = MAX_SIZE - 1 = 2^59 - 1; reached from regionFromStride in AccessLogs.readWord/writeWord/readLeaf/writeLeaf
candidates.description: The tree has 2^59 leaves (strides 0..2^59-1). validateStrideLength requires stride*size < 2^59 - 1, so for size 1 it refuses stride 2^59-1, the leaf 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE0..0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, with a Panic(0x01). The C++ side has no such restriction: machine::read_word there returns zeros (pristine padding) and the C++ replay verifies the leaf proof. So a uarch step whose load or instruction fetch hits the last leaf is a valid transition with a canonical after-hash that every C++ path computes and proves, while the referee rejects its honest log. Any region whose last leaf is the top leaf is refused the same way (larger regions are fine because stride*s = 2^59 - s < 2^59 - 1).
candidates.trigger: Any party proving a uarch step from a before-state where the uarch reads (ld/lw/lb..., or fetches an instruction) at an address in the top 32 bytes of the 64-bit space; e.g. 'ld x1,-8(x0)'.
candidates.reachability: Believed unreachable from a valid template: every address range is limited to 56 bits (machine_address_ranges::check: 'must use at most 56 bits to be addressable'), and the pristine uarch program only touches the uarch state, the shadow state and physical memory that its PMA/TLB checks place inside a range, so it never reads the top leaf. Reachable only with a non-pristine uarch (or corrupted cached TLB/PMA indices, R10), none of which a valid template produces.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no; it concerns the referee verifier's acceptance of a log.
2 Role: Referee verifier (AUDIT.md: machine-solidity-step regenerated | Referee verifier); the C++ verifier/producer that disagree are Support/Honest operator.

3 High/Medium cases: High: 'A divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states.' R2 requires 'Every log producer and every log verifier' and 'The on-chain verifiers' to agree; R3: 'A verifier must never turn ... a semantic no-op into a rejection' (here a semantic successor into a rejection); R10: the verifier must remain deterministic/safe on every before-state. Unreachability argued above.

4 Critical: would be Critical (R4 'From any reachable state ... log the transition so that it verifies'; completeness failure of section 1) if any reachable uarch access touched the top leaf; none known.
candidates.threat_to_goal: The referee does not implement the state transition function on its whole domain; correctness then rests on the extra, undocumented invariant that no reachable uarch access touches the top leaf. If that ever failed (e.g. a uarch program or layout change), the honest claim could not prove its step on-chain and would lose (completeness failure).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R3/lastleaf.lua: uarch_pc -> 'ld x1,-8(x0)' on a 1 MiB machine. m:log_step_uarch() succeeds (x1=0), cartesi.machine:verify_step_uarch reproduces the after-hash, but the regenerated StepVerifier.step reverts with 'panic: assertion failed (0x01)'. Control 'ld x1,-40(x0)' (previous leaf) verifies on-chain with the same hash as native. Memory.sol is byte-identical in released v0.17.0-test1, regenerated-patched and Dave's machine/step.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: produce the log for 'ld x1,-8(x0)' with log_step_uarch, require that the EVM step (or CartesiStateTransition on the released Dave build) returns the same after-hash as verify_step_uarch; exit 1 while it reverts.

candidates.title: Referee model (prt.lua validate_state_transition_response) accepts state-transition proofs carrying superfluous logs (send_cmio_log without a delivery, reset_uarch_log on a non-closing step) and ignores them
candidates.component: doc/recipes/prt.lua validate_state_transition_response (also reproduced in doc/README.md); prt-ethereum.lua verify_transition (support) likewise
candidates.description: The response to ProveStateTransition may contain send_cmio_log, step_log and reset_uarch_log (prtu.lua schema). The model only reads send_cmio_log at an input-slot opening that holds an input, and reset_uarch_log at the last uarch cycle; otherwise those fields are silently ignored and the proof is accepted. The deployed referee (Dave CartesiStateTransition) concatenates the logs into one buffer and requires exact consumption, so it rejects the same proof as trailing data. The model and the deployed referee thus disagree on what a referee accepts, and the model accepts trailing data contrary to R3 ('A log that fails one must be rejected. Examples are ... duplicate, missing, or trailing data').
candidates.trigger: Any claimant answering prove_state_transition with an extra log field.
candidates.reachability: Reachable at every leaf match of the PRT recipe; no machine state needed.
rating_steps: 2 Role: Referee model ('The PRT referee model in doc/recipes | Referee model'); 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.'
3 High/Medium cases: Medium: 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3).' The extra logs do not change the after-hash.
4 Critical: no, the result is unaffected.
5 Low: would be Low only if one reads the superfluous fields as not being part of the proof; triage decides.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not affect the settled state; it violates R3's log-validity condition and makes the normative model more permissive than the deployed referee, so proofs the model accepts can be refused on-chain (a player tested only against the model could submit them).
candidates.evidence: Code reading only (prt.lua 278-291: the optional logs are consulted only under their position conditions; no check that they are absent otherwise).
candidates.test_idea: Call the model's validation (or run a leaf match in prt-test style) with a valid honest response plus a reset_uarch_log on a non-closing uarch cycle, or a send_cmio_log at a non-delivery position, and require rejection; exit 1 while it returns the after-hash.

not_covered: Arithmetic/semantic equivalence of every generated UArchStep.sol instruction against uarch-step.cpp beyond what the 56 replay tests cover (no differential fuzzing run).
